svg.text: Three layers, left to right: what people use, the data it stands on, and the gateway and governance every request passes through — on the platform's shared observability stack

forms and voice — what people use
Five scenario kinds, one service instance per kind, each
rendered by generic tabs plus an optional showpiece tab (maps,
networks, globes). A scenario is a YAML file: content, never
capture → store → transform → serve; trains the models and indexes the documents
Left: the streaming path of a data product, in order (optional tiers: core, analytics, bi, governance). Right: batch jobs that train
models and index documents, and the stores everything lives in — all scoped by org_id.

The entitlement check happens in the backend, never only in the
UI. Governance-ready by standards, everything off by default:
it supports a management system — it is not one.
shared by everything on the Kubernetes cluster — a prerequisite the framework plugs into, not part of it (ADR 0015)
• OTLP traces when the platform sets an endpoint
• JSON logs with trace_id and span_id
• no prompts or personal data in spans or logs:
those stay in Langfuse, linked by trace id

The framework ships only its side: the contract above, then AI dashboards (gateway tokens, cost and latency, GPU, model drift), alert rules, a collector snippet and an optional lab bundle, off by default.
Dashed border = optional. See architecture-detailed.svg for every service-to-service call and architecture-data-platform.svg for the data path in detail.
